item.title: Mississippi man sentenced to 30 years in prison for setting fire to LDS church
item.description: A Mississippi man was sentenced to 30 years in prison for setting fire to a church building belonging to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in 2024.

item.title: Utah reaches 251 measles cases total, with 56 cases this year
item.description: As of an updated count released on Tuesday, Utah has reached 251 measles cases during this current outbreak, with 56 of those cases being diagnosed in 2026.

item.title: Switchpoint opens expansion in St. George, adding 16 rooms for families experiencing homelessness
item.description: Switchpoint just opened its new family expansion unit in St. George, providing additional rooms so families experiencing homelessness can stay together, something that is much needed in Southern Utah, as Washington County's homelessness rate is higher than the state average.

item.title: Motorcyclist critically injured after crash in Holladay
item.description: One is critically injured after a crash in Holladay on Tuesday evening.

item.title: South Salt Lake Police looking for missing 60-year-old not seen by family for a year
item.description: South Salt Lake Police are looking for help in locating a missing man who has not been seen by his family since February of last year.

item.title: Trial to go forward against man who allegedly tortured, killed wolf
item.description: A Wyoming man is set to go to trial next month for allegedly torturing and killing a wolf in 2024, after a judge denied his motion to dismiss the case altogether.

item.title: Southern Utah family expresses concern after child's smart watch overheats
item.description: A Utah family is concerned after they say their son's smart watch overheated and started to burn.

item.title: Superstar skier Lindsey Vonn planning to compete in Winter Games despite ACL injury
item.description: It may be the year's biggest comeback if Utah Olympic Skier Lindsey Vonn is able to compete in the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics, which start Sunday.

item.title: Lake Powell residents express concerns over water levels due to low snowpack
item.description: With water levels at Lake Powell sitting at 27% and record low snowpack in Utah, residents and boaters are concerned about potential implications for the lake.

item.title: 'The Constitution applies to everyone': Immigration lawyer condemns recent border patrol arrests in West Valley City
item.description: On Friday, Jan. 30, U.S. Border Patrol reportedly detained two individuals in West Valley City after entering a business without a judicial warrant. The lawyer for one of those individuals spoke on why the arrests have been so controversial and why they may be unconstitutional.
